description: 4-track stereo mixer with a level, a ducker, mute and solo on each track, a 8-band master equaliser, and a chain input so several mixers can feed one output

params.text: Sets that track's gain, silent at the bottom of its travel, unity in the middle and twice over at the top
Sets how hard the jack below it pulls that track down: nothing at the bottom of its travel, and at the top a third of ten volts is enough to silence the track
Silences that track, and lights while the track is silent, whether by this button or by another track in the chain being soloed
Silences every other track in the chain of mixers this one is touching; held down for 400ms it also clears every other solo in that chain
Lifts or cuts the master mix around that band's centre, -12dB to +12dB, with the centre frequency printed under it

inputs.text: The left side of that track; with nothing patched to the right jack beside it this one feeds both sides, the right delayed by 20ms to widen it
The right side of that track
Added to that track's LEVEL knob, a tenth of the knob's travel per volt; the total is held between silence and twice over
Pulls that track down as its voltage rises, 0V leaving it alone and 10V ducking it as far as the DUCK knob allows
A rising edge through 1V toggles that track's mute button
A rising edge through 1V toggles that track's solo button
A signal added into the left mix after the tracks and before the equaliser
A signal added into the right mix after the tracks and before the equaliser

outputs.text: The left side of the tracks and the chain input, through the equaliser and clipped at ±10V
The right side of the tracks and the chain input, through the equaliser and clipped at ±10V

notes: solo reaches across the rack. Every U8, ALEXANDERPLATZ and SHINJUKU touching this one is searched, and a track not soloed is silenced while a solo is on anywhere in that run.
place a YAMANOTE immediately to the left and its mix output is cabled into the two chain jacks on its own, in the YAMANOTE green.
the equaliser bands are fixed at 63Hz, 125Hz, 250Hz, 500Hz, 1000Hz, 2000Hz, 4000Hz and 8000Hz and only their gains can be moved.
